original_question: (T. Breuer, R. M. Guralnick). Let G be a finite simple group and let p1, p2 be any(not necessarily distinct) prime divisors of |G|. Then can we always find Sylow pi-subgroups Hi such that G = ⟨H1, H2 ⟩?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.25 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)": "(T. Breuer, R. M. Guralnick). Let G be a finite simple group and let p1, p2 be any (not necessarily distinct) prime divisors of |G|. Then can we always find Sylow pi-subgroups Hi such that G = ⟨H1, H2⟩?"
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the official problem almost verbatim: the ambient class is finite simple groups; the primes p_1 and p_2 are allowed to coincide; they are required to divide |G|; and the question asks whether one can choose Sylow p_1- and p_2-subgroups whose generated subgroup is all of G.
missing_details: Make the quantifiers fully explicit: the question is for every finite simple group G and every choice of prime divisors p_1, p_2 of |G|.
Specify that for each i = 1, 2, H_i is a Sylow p_i-subgroup of G.
Clarify that G = ⟨H_1, H_2⟩ means that H_1 and H_2 together generate G.
refined_question: For every finite simple group G and every pair of prime divisors p_1, p_2 of |G|, allowing p_1 = p_2, do there exist Sylow p_i-subgroups H_i ≤ G for i = 1, 2 such that G = ⟨H_1, H_2⟩?
justification: The draft is essentially the exact official formulation of Problem 21.25. In this paper, the relevant target is not a theorem or conjecture in an introduction but a standalone open problem entry, and there is no narrower paper-faithful reformulation nearby. So the sharpest refinement is to preserve the statement while making the universal quantifiers and the role of the Sylow p_i-subgroups explicit.
